question.problem:
Find, **in radians**, the **exact value** of the argument of $z=6-6\text{i}.$

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$ 

$\operatorname{arg}⁡(z)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226152/assets/7cdd04a6728120c66f4befafeb5a0bf2f053c8ed0ed2c1014e87549820e5c3ac.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant of the complex plane. Hence $\frac{3\pi }{2}<\operatorname{arg}⁡(z)<2\pi .$ 

If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the positive real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\alpha  & =\frac{6}{6} \\ \alpha  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z)=2\pi -\frac{\pi }{4}=\frac{7\pi }{4}.
$$
